question: It is characteristic of the epithelia:

options.opa: Present a binding complex in its basal region.
options.opb: Join the basement membrane by means of hemidesmosomes and focal adhesions.
options.opc: Present desmosomes just below its free surface.
options.opd: Contain intermediate filaments of vimentin and desmin (tonofilaments)

analysis: Epithelial cells are known to connect to the basement membrane through structures like hemidesmosomes and focal adhesions. These structures help anchor the epithelial cells to the underlying connective tissue. Desmosomes are typically found on the lateral surfaces of epithelial cells, not just below the free surface. Intermediate filaments in epithelial cells are usually composed of keratin, not vimentin and desmin, which are found in mesenchymal cells and muscle cells, respectively.
